attack: The skeptic’s ‘already delivered / untradeable’ map is a 1y-post-FOMC story. It fits US 2s10s at the 56th 5y percentile and USDCAD at the 71st 1y percentile. It does not fit AUDNZD at the 99.96th 5y percentile still grinding higher the day after housing and FTA news.

USD expressions (NZDUSD, AUDUSD, USDCAD) own residual dollar beta after futures assigned >90% odds to the 16 Sep 25bp hike to 3.75–4.00%. The discrepancy is Oceania-relative: rich AUDUSD versus cheap NZDUSD. Putting USD in the book re-imports a spent event.

USDCAD/CA-US seats misread a fundamental Canada-US policy gap (core near 2%, labor 38 versus 75, 139bp 2Y cheapness) as FX mispricing that must close in spot. Comparable-country normalization rejects CAD as the AUD peer because energy/ToT and a verified CA-AU 2Y yield giveaway contaminate that identity.

AU duration and AU-US 2Y are the same housing story with a worse overlay: inflation gauge 82, eight-day-stale pre-FOMC yields, and a milder z_5y +1.43 versus AUDNZD z_5y +2.96. Express the trade where the mispricing lives.

A straddle on unobserved IV is an implementation dodge, not a valuation argument. Directional spot is the object that owns the 5y peer premium colliding with housing transmission and an NZ export impulse.
concession_trigger: An official NZ 2Y/5Y/10Y print showing an AU yield premium consistent with AUDNZD z_5y +2.96 as carry/policy, or AU housing volumes/prices/stamp-duty stabilizing while NZ labor/activity remain the weaker side without an offsetting AU slowdown.
defense: Verified fact: AU and NZ inflation gauges are 82 and 80, so the cross extreme is not a PPP-like inflation gap. The valuation anchor is peer-normalized spot history plus that inflation match, not a post-drop dip-buy.

Verified fact: the closing mechanism is change, not the percentile alone. NSW stamp-duty receipts fell 24% YoY, volumes fell 18%, Sydney/Melbourne values are more than 7% off peak (2026-09-16), and NZ parliament cut tariffs on about 95% of NZ exports to India the same day. Convergence should start now because 17 Sep AUDNZD is still priced as if AU can keep delivering that premium after the housing hole printed.

Inference: NZ real-side weakness is already in NZDUSD at the 5y 11.5th percentile. The residual is AUD richness versus that peer, not an unpriced NZ recession. Stock versus change is the hole in the ‘NZ is weaker so the cross is fair’ claim.

Unknown: REER/PPP, terms of trade, current accounts, executable bid/offer, and AU-NZ yields. Those gaps cut confidence; they do not authorize inventing NZ yields or migrating into a milder USD/rates object.

Rates comparison still loses: outright AU duration is inflation-contaminated; AU 2s10s is not extreme (pctile_5y 32.301587301587304); matched AU-NZ RV is unavailable and must stay null. Spot remains the cleaner value expression.
holes_in_opposing_case: no-trade-skeptic treats missing NZ yields and non-executable ECB FX as a veto on the packet’s largest verified 5y FX extreme. Research method says missing data haircuts confidence; it is not permission to ignore a 99.96th-percentile 5y cross with dated closers. AUDNZD is a 5y extreme (pctile_5y 99.96031746031746, z_5y 2.956392537701696), not a 1y-vs-5y median artifact like US 2s10s (1y ~1.4th / 5y ~56th). ECB non-executability is common to every spot seat, not unique to this cross.

perma-bull long NZDUSD owns a spent USD residual after a >90%-priced 16 Sep 25bp hike. The 1m split is already AUDUSD +0.5375457114422666 versus NZDUSD -2.33032315295707; buying cheap NZD versus USD without selling rich AUD leaves AUDNZD z_5y +2.96 unowned. US activity 69 / labor 75 does not explain why AUD should remain at a 5y-max versus NZD after NSW stamp-duty receipts fell 24% YoY. above_trend/risk_on collides with NZ labor 32 and the AU housing hole.

perma-bear short AUDUSD attacks the wrong object: AUDUSD is only pctile_1y 74.8015873015873 / pctile_5y 83.53174603174604, not the dislocation. Short AUDUSD contaminates the housing closer with a delivered, >90%-priced Fed hike (AUDUSD already -0.990713617083816 over 5d). Calling NZ the weaker economy confuses stock already in NZDUSD pctile_5y 11.468253968253968 with change dated 16 Sep (housing + India FTA) against a still-rising 17 Sep AUDNZD (ret_1d +0.08908453918168302, ret_1m +2.936294003399431). Inflation gauges 82 versus 80 reject an inflation-gap justification for the cross extreme.

dollar-king and carry-is-king long USDCAD substitute a milder USD pair for the historical FX extreme. USDCAD is only pctile_1y 70.83333333333333 / pctile_5y 86.23015873015873 (spot 1.399529657695323), z_5y 0.956, versus AUDNZD z_5y 2.956. CA-US 2Y -139bp (pctile_5y 4.670999187652315) and CA-US 5Y -122bp (pctile_1y 0.1984126984126984, pctile_5y 7.35174654752234) coexist with CA core near 2% and labor 38 versus US 75 — that gap is at least partly fundamental, which is why fading it is not a convergence trade. Verified CA-AU 2Y -167.5bp (pctile_5y 8.591205211726384) argues against expressing AU housing by shorting AUD via CAD, not against AUDNZD, which has no verified rate anchor. Unknown AUDNZD carry is a haircut, not a reason to replace a 5y-max peer cross with a 71st-percentile 1y USD pair.

rate-dove receive-ACGB versus pay-UST owns a weaker stretch: AU-US 2Y +40.5bp as of 2026-09-09 is only pctile_5y 89.07528641571194 / z_5y 1.433030874747196, and those AU yields are eight days stale and pre-FOMC. AU inflation gauge 82 plus a live Fed/ECB hike wave makes long AU duration inflation-contaminated. The structure ignores NZDUSD already at the 5y 11.5th percentile. An easing_cycle assumption overreaches inflation 82.

rate-hawk pay-CAN versus receive-UST treats a BoC energy-pass-through warning as catch-up already owed while CA labor is 38 and core is near 2%. The Saudi-Oman workaround reduced the oil-supply tail that would force that catch-up. This RV does not own AUDNZD z_5y +2.96. Fading a 5y-cheap CA-US spread without a delivered BoC hike is the statistical trap rejected in round 1.

trend-follower pay UST 5Y and catalyst-junkie pay US 2Y are inflation-path speculation after a delivered, >90%-priced hike and a 17 Sep 7–8bp yield dip. Neither owns the Oceania peer dislocation. AU housing is the packet’s only hard tightening-channel print; paying UST does not express it.

vol-convexity’s 1-month ATM straddle cannot be shown to be the cleaner expression: implied vol, skew, and premium are unobserved, and their own invalidation is stand-down if live IV is rich to rv_20d 4.831979728655883 / rv_60d 5.132596494753644. Two-way tails overstate the stock of NZ weakness versus one-way change (AU housing deterioration plus NZ FTA). A continued ~5 realized-vol grind is theta death for the straddle and is exactly when a directional fade of a 5y extreme can work. Unknown IV is not unusually compelling versus spot.

cross-merchant, mean-reverter, and positioning-cynic do not oppose short AUDNZD; they share the instrument. positioning_and_flow is empty, so crowding is an inference from percentiles, not measured inventories. The valuation identity does not require CTA ownership to be observed.

catalysts: Further AU housing/transaction/fiscal-receipt deterioration that forces relative RBA restraint versus current AUD richness.
Market pricing of the NZ-India FTA as a durable NZ export impulse.
Any official NZ yield print that shows AU-NZ rate differentials too small to justify a 5y-max AUDNZD.

revised_trade.expression: Fade historically rich AUD versus NZD in spot: sell AUDNZD on the 2026-09-17 ECB euro-reference cross.
revised_trade.horizon: 1–3 months tactical; 3–6 months for peer-spread convergence
revised_trade.invalidation: Thesis is wrong if an official NZ government-bond yield print shows an AU-NZ differential large enough to justify a 5y-max AUDNZD as carry/policy premium, or if the AU housing channel reverses (volumes/prices/stamp-duty stabilize) while NZ labor/activity remain the weaker side without an offsetting AU slowdown. Do not use an invented price stop.
revised_trade.mispricing: AUD is historically expensive versus NZD on the five-year distribution (spot 1.2388004213396122, pctile_5y 99.96031746031746, z_5y 2.956392537701696, pctile_1y 99.8015873015873, z_1y 1.7049400389512894). That is a peer-spread dislocation, not a one-sided crash. AU-NZ bond RV cannot confirm or reject a rates justification because NZ official yields are unavailable. No REER/PPP levels are in the packet; the anchor is the historical G10 cross distribution plus relative temperature gauges and the housing/FTA catalysts. USDCAD (pctile_1y 70.83333333333333 / pctile_5y 86.23015873015873) and AUDUSD (pctile_1y 74.8015873015873 / pctile_5y 83.53174603174604) are not this extreme.
principal_risks: NZ real-side gauges are already weaker than AU (labor 32 vs 50, consumer 38 vs 48, activity 47 vs 54), which can justify some AUD premium and keep the cross rich.
Inflation gauges remain hot in both (AU 82, NZ 80); a renewed AU inflation scare can extend AUD richness.
NZ rates are missing, so short AUDNZD may be short the high-yielder with negative carry.
Temperature gauges are dashboard-retained/stale; AU yields are eight days old; ECB FX is not executable.
Global Fed/ECB tightening and energy-inflation residual can keep commodity FX in a USD-driven regime that delays peer convergence.
revised_trade.structure: outright spot FX; short AUD / long NZD
revised_trade.thesis: The valuation anchor is peer-normalized spot history, not the fact that anything sold off: AUDNZD is at the 99.96th five-year percentile (z_5y +2.96) with AUDUSD already rich (5y 83.5th) and NZDUSD already cheap (5y 11.5th). Comparable-country inflation gauges are similar (AU 82 vs NZ 80), so that extreme AUD premium is not a PPP-like inflation gap. NZ labor/activity/consumer weakness is the stock already in cheap NZDUSD; the change that should compress the residual AUD premium is NSW stamp-duty receipts −24% YoY, volumes −18%, and Sydney/Melbourne values more than 7% below peak, plus NZ’s India FTA cutting tariffs on about 95% of NZ exports. USD pairs, AU duration, CA-US RV, and an unobserved-IV straddle do not own that peer dislocation. Convergence should start now because the 17 Sep cross is still priced as if AU can keep delivering the yield/FX premium after that housing hole is visible.
why_now: AUDNZD is already at the top of the five-year sample and still printed ret_1d +0.08908453918168302 on 2026-09-17 after 16 Sep housing and FTA news, so entry is statistically stretched after the discrepancy is identified, not instead of it.
AU housing is the new transmission: stamp-duty and transaction collapse is the tightening channel showing up in real activity/fiscal receipts, which should compress the AUD premium versus NZD.
NZ parliament passing the India trade agreement is independent NZ-side fundamental news that does not belong with a record-rich AUDNZD.

AU outright yields are also historically high, but AU inflation 82, eight-day-stale pre-FOMC AU yields, and a live global hike wave make long AU duration a dirtier expression of the same housing story. USD pairs re-import a >90%-priced FOMC residual.

strongest_opponent_point: NZ labor/consumer/activity gauges are already weaker than Australia (32/38/47 versus 50/48/54) and official NZ yields are unavailable (RBNZ B2 HTTP 403), so the AUDNZD 5y extreme can be a fair NZ-growth/carry premium rather than a peer mispricing; fading it is then un-risk-matched and possibly negative-carry, and sitting out or substituting USDCAD/AUDUSD/NZDUSD/AU duration/vol is cleaner.
unresolved_question: Whether the unobserved AU-NZ government-bond differential already pays for a 5y-max AUDNZD, because RBNZ B2 remains HTTP 403 and REER/PPP/ToT/external balances are also absent.
